transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-14 09:30 UTC | Duration: ~74 minutes
Location: Zoom (internal)
Attendees: Dana Liu, Ethan Brooks, Priya Nair, Jorge Alvarez, Leah Kim, Marcus Chen, Ava Roberts

Summary: Quick planning session to solidify capacity runway assumptions for the next six weeks and pick 2-3 quick wins that materially reduce token-cost or latency during launch. Also to stress test fallback and canary gating for Dedicated vs Hosted rollouts.

Topics (auto): capacity runway, KV eviction, canary thresholds, quick-win tickets, fallback runbook, release gating

Transcript: (timestamps approx every 30-60s; transcription imperfect)
00:00 Dana: okay, um hi everyone thanks for carving out time, we're pressing on the capacity runway question for Q1 and there's a few quick wins we think can buy us runway without requiring more reserved capacity
00:18 Marcus: yeah, and we need clarity on the gating — if the runway shortens we need to know what we flip first latency or throughput or cost?
00:30 Ethan: my view is latency-first for customer-facing chat flows, but for batch embedding jobs we can trade latency for cost, so the plan should be route-by-policy as we talked about - sorry if that echoes the deck
00:45 Priya: quick thing, the KV-eviction spike from last sim two weeks ago still shows a memory cliff at 48k tokens, so if we surface that in canaries we might catch it, but our sim needs more realistic prefix reuse - the transcription here: "prefix re-use" might be spelled wrong in the notes
01:12 Jorge: yeah, and the kernel fallback path currently adds ~23ms; on paper that's fine but during sustained load that accumulates, um so the fallback runbook needs to specify when to switch models vs when to adjust batch windows
01:40 Ava: can we also please make sure audit and logging bits are in the runbook? security wants an easy repro for any degraded-run incidents, and SOC2 audit docs should map to those steps
01:58 Dana: good call Ava; Leah can you add a checkbox for audit log capture in the runbook template?
02:09 Leah: noted, I will. also I'll lock the runway testing dates the week of 2/2 so we have space after the feature freeze
02:27 Marcus: i'd like a quick sanity check — what are the assumptions on traffic growth? last run was 18% week over week; is that baked in?
02:40 Ethan: we used conservative 12% w/w in the model — because some of the marketing promos dropped off — but we can re-run with 18% if leadership wants, it's just more pessimistic
03:05 Priya: action item — i'll run two sim variants: one with 12% and one with 18, and also one with a higher cache hit rate to show best-case. i think the key is KV cache miss behavior across multi-tenant workloads
03:30 Jorge: small nit — the current quant profile we used for the benchmark may have mis-tagged a layer, so the numbers for A100 look optimistic, need a re-quant run on the model with seq len 1024
03:55 Dana: ok so quick-wins candidate list: (1) batch-window tuning + dynamic batch sizing, (2) KV-prefetch heuristic improvement, (3) lower-precision quant profile for background models. which two should we prioritize?
04:18 Ethan: I'd prioritize batch tuning and KV-prefetch. batch tuning has immediate perf wins across hosts and is lower risk. KV-prefetch might reduce tail latency for interactive sessions
04:36 Marcus: agree. but ensure the preftech doesn't increase memory footprint beyond the eviction cliff 
04:50 Priya: right — my sim will show that. also, if we do preftech we need eviction thresholds to tolerate +10% memory for a short rolling window
05:10 Jorge: for the fallback runbook we should codify triggers: CPU/GPU utilization > 88% for 5 min, token service error rate > 0.5% sustained for 3 min, and KV miss-rate spike > X. those are placeholders but we should align on numbers
05:40 Dana: let's capture those thresholds as draft; Leah can we make a shared doc and pin it?
05:50 Leah: yes i'll create the doc and template the runbook with sections: triggers, decision flow, owner matrix, audit steps, rollback criteria
06:12 Ava: and include compliance owners for any data-retention or KMS calls — don't assume SRE will do it alone
06:25 Priya: another ops note — if we fallback to a smaller model family we need a precedent for re-routing requests to dedicated pool vs hosted pool; the routing policy must be explicit. we have an earlier note about automatic fallback to compatible variants but it's fuzzy
06:52 Jorge: i can draft the routing policy bullets — i want to make sure we mention region-aware fallbacks (EU vs US), since some customers will prefer regional consistency
07:10 Marcus: also: pricing/commerce dimension — if we degrade to lower-quality model we need comms templates for CS and legal prepared in advance
07:25 Dana: good — Leah can you add a comms template item to the checklist?
07:36 Leah: yes i'll add two templates: internal incident comms and customer-facing degraded-performance note
07:50 Ethan: on the technical side, two quick experiments: one is a smaller micro-batching change that reduces lock contention in the serving runtime, second is a kernel selection cache warmup during canary ramp. both low-effort? estimate 3-4 dev days each
08:14 Jorge: micro-batching is higher risk if request sizes vary widely, we need to tune the greedy window and add timeouts to avoid head-of-line blocking
08:33 Priya: tie that to SLO experiments — during canary we run A/B with micro-batching on 20% traffic for 48 hours and compare p50/p95/p99
08:50 Dana: note: canary thresholds must include business-side metrics, not just latency. set success criterion: p50 within 5% of baseline, error rate not increased more than 0.1% and token cost per request not increased more than 3%
09:20 Marcus: what about the canary monitoring pipeline — do we have dashboards ready to ingest the additional KPIs?
09:32 Ethan: Leah and I will pick the dashboard metrics; we may need an extra log ingestion lambda to pull KV miss traces to the observability stack for the early canary phase
09:48 Priya: i want to highlight a risk: the prefix cache serialization format change we did last quarter could make old KV indices invalid in a mixed-version deploy. if we can freeze that for the canary and run a conversion step in the background, it reduces risk
10:10 Jorge: good call. if the conversion is heavy we should schedule it in a dedicated maintenance window, not during canary ramp
10:31 Dana: ok, let's enumerate deliverables and owners now — quick round-robin: Priya?
10:37 Priya: run KV-eviction sims (12%/18% traffic) + test preftech memory footprint. deliverable: spreadsheet + topline summary. due 2026-01-21
10:52 Ethan: scope batch-window tuning ticket and canary dashboard metrics; estimate 8 dev days split across two engineers. deliverable: two PRs + dashboard. due 2026-01-18
11:10 Jorge: draft fallback runbook and routing policy bullets with region-awareness and owner matrix. deliverable: runbook draft in doc. due 2026-01-19
11:34 Leah: update release calendar, create runbook template and comms templates, create doc and pin in drive. due 2026-01-16
11:55 Dana: i'll update the launch gate checklist to include the new thresholds and make sure the canary success criteria are explicit. due 2026-01-20
12:10 Ava: please include SOC2 contact and KMS checklist in that doc; i'll follow up with compliance owners
12:25 Marcus: one last ask — can we run a short smoke benchmark with the current quant profiles but with seq len 1024? i'd like to see the regression numbers before we commit to quant changes
12:40 Jorge: yes i'll run a quick quant re-eval and post numbers; it's a low-effort compile job but the run could take a few hours on the infra side
12:58 Dana: great, thanks everyone. recap of next steps posted in the doc. any final comments?
13:06 Ethan: tiny note — maybe we also do a short tabletop with oncall next Tuesday to walk through the fallback runbook so they're not surprised
13:18 Priya: agree, schedule it in the oncall rota please
13:30 Dana: ok Leah will book a 30-min tabletop with oncall and SRE next Tuesday. meeting adjourned.
